provenance.statement: Contracts/spfn-mobile-contract.json is a byte copy of contracts/mobile/spfn-mobile-contract.json as published by SPFN primitives at the commit named below. It is generated there from packages/auth/src/server/client-proof by packages/auth/scripts/export-mobile-contract.ts, and it is not edited here.
provenance.whyThisIsAnUpstreamPin: A digest is only worth pinning when it names a file an independent party produced. This digest names a file SPFN primitives generated from its own route and contract definitions, so it is evidence about the server. The dev bundle it replaces proved only that this repository's generator and both SDKs read the same local bytes, which is self-verification.
provenance.evidence: Contracts/upstream-provenance.json, copied unmodified from the same upstream commit. The contract's own facts — name, version, major, supportedRange and bundleSha256 — live there and only there; this lock does not restate them, so there is nothing here to compare against them.
provenance.editRule: This bundle is never edited here. A contract change is made in SPFN primitives, re-exported there, and re-pinned here as a new commit and a new digest.

source.keyNamingRule: This is not called bundlePath on purpose. The readers of this file match a key name at any depth, so two keys with the same name in different objects would resolve to whichever appears first, and the validator would digest the upstream path instead of the vendored one.

publishedPackages.rule: The npm versions published from source.commit. A commit is not something npm can install, and nothing in an installed @spfn/auth says which contract it implements — the bundle is not shipped in the package and neither is the code that builds it. So the mapping from a package version to a contract version exists only here, written by hand from the commit history, and tools/verify-server/run.sh compares an app's installed tree against it.
publishedPackages.registryRule: The @spfn/auth 0.3.0-beta.8 and @spfn/core 0.3.0-beta.6 releases are published in the Superfunction Gitea registry. A machine whose npmrc scopes @spfn elsewhere can resolve a different line, and --registry does not override a scope: use --@spfn:registry for an explicit comparison. tools/verify-server/spfn-versions.sh asks both configured registries and refuses to answer with a single number.
publishedPackages.peerRangeWarning: @spfn/auth declares @spfn/core >=0.2.0-beta.54, which a much older core satisfies while lacking the error envelope this contract's codes ride in. The consumer pins @spfn/core exactly rather than letting resolution choose.

contract.name: spfn-mobile-contract
contract.pathRule: Where the vendored copy lives in THIS repository, which is the one contract fact no upstream file can state: the exporter knows its own tree, not the consumer's. Everything else about the contract — version, major, supportedRange, bundleSha256 — is read from Contracts/upstream-provenance.json.

digestDiscipline.rule: Contracts/upstream-provenance.json's contract.bundleSha256 must be the real SHA-256 of the file named by contract.bundlePath above. tools/validate/validate.sh recomputes it, and tools/contract-codegen refuses to generate when it does not match, so a tampered bundle fails on both paths rather than producing plausible clients.

notes: lockVersion 3 (2026-09-18) removed contract.version, major, minor, manifestSha256, supportedRange and rangeRule, which restated Contracts/upstream-provenance.json, and authProfiles, which is an SDK policy whose home is SPFNAuthProfile/SpfnAuthProfile and tools/validate/validate.sh section 6. Every reader of a removed value now reads upstream-provenance.json; the checks that compared the two copies are gone because there is no second copy to disagree.

What is left is what only the consumer knows: which primitives commit was read, which npm versions were published from it, where the vendored bundle sits in this tree, and the rules for editing all three.
Floating branches or URLs are prohibited as a lock source; only an exact repository, commit SHA and exporter version.
A published contract version and digest are never modified. A mistake becomes a new version.
The bundle carries no secret and no real private key.
